laws.rule: Shenzhen: smoking is banned in indoor workplaces, indoor public places and public transport, and in listed outdoor areas, including outdoor parts of parks, tourist attractions, museums and heritage sites outside designated smoking points, within 5 metres of public transport station entrances, and in outdoor spectator areas of sports venues. The regulation defines smoking to include using an e-cigarette and holding a lit or heated tobacco product.
laws.penalty_signal: Individuals: CNY 50 fine on the spot, CNY 200 if they refuse to comply, CNY 500 if they obstruct enforcement (about A$11, A$43 and A$107). Rate: A$1 = CNY 4.6877, RBA 30 Oct 2026.

laws.rule: Guangzhou: smoking is banned in 12 kinds of place, including indoor service areas of government and public-service bodies, shops, bookshops and the indoor business areas of banks, post and telecom firms, and in office corridors and lifts. Larger restaurants may keep a smoking room.
laws.penalty_signal: Individuals who refuse to stop: CNY 50 (about A$11). The regulation took effect 1 Sept 2019; a revision is on the city's 2022 to 2026 legislative plan, so check the current text.
